content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I need some help. We recently had to replace our previous [product_name] with a newer [product_name] due to supply issues. Since making this change, I'm having trouble monitoring the temperature inputs. The reading is constant and doesn't update. I was under the impression these modules were compatible, but there seem to be subtle differences causing issues. As part of the transition, we also upgraded [product_name] software from [version_no] to [version_no] after initial communication problems with the new hardware. Thank you in advance! [user_name]

Hi [user_name], A few important tips: 1) Make sure your [product_name] software is updated to the latest version. This will allow you to work with all devices. - Use the UPDATE CENTER from the HELP menu - Choose to update from the INTERNET (with a valid connection) - The required [url] will already be set - You'll see all available updates for your installed version. Select the latest one (e.g., [version_no] or similar). 2) After updating, confirm the version under HELP > ABOUT. It should display [version_no]. 3) Next, set your target device. In the bottom right, double-click on it. - Select [product_name] version [version_no] (check your packaging for the exact version). 4) Now you will be able to program and transfer data to the device without any issues. 5) Regarding analog inputs: The newer [product_name] allows up to 4 onboard digital inputs to function as analog (0-10V), while the older version only supports 2. Using an older configuration file with the new hardware will cause input assignment issues and unexpected behavior. 6) To fix this: Go to FILE > PROPERTIES > PARAMETER page. Here, you can configure the number of onboard analog inputs. Set it to 2 for compatibility with the older version. This should resolve your problems! ["Wishing you a great day!"]

Thank you for your advice. I am now able to toggle between all four analog inputs by applying voltage to each one. My setup includes two temperature sensors (PT100) connected via the [product_name] expansion module. What I don't understand is why the system isn't reading values from the expansion module but is only picking up the onboard inputs. Is it possible that the main module isn't configured to detect the expansion module, or do the analog inputs need to be mapped to the PT100 sensors?

Problem solved—the expansion module wasn't correctly connected; the interface hadn't fully joined with the main unit. After fixing the installation, everything started working as expected. Thank you for your assistance.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encountered confusion and misconfiguration when upgrading to a new hardware version of [product_name]. Challenges included differences in analog input mapping and module compatibility, compounded by uncertainty about hardware and software setup and expansion module detection. The issue was ultimately resolved by correcting a hardware connection, underscoring the importance of clear setup procedures.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect easy compatibility during hardware migration, clear analog input mapping, and reliable identification of expansion modules and sensors.
